previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE was admitted for severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Initial concern for infection or bowel ischemia was ruled out with imaging and labs. A CT scan showed a new hypodense lesion in the liver corresponding to the recent TACE site, consistent with post-TACE inflammation. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, including IV fluids, anti-nausea medications, and pain control. She was restarted on her liver medications, including lactulose and spironolactone, and received prophylactic diazepam due to mild alcohol withdrawal symptoms. Her condition stabilized, she advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home in improved condition with follow-up arranged with her hepatologist and primary care provider.

cirrhosis.  Evaluate for acute intra-abdominal abnormality

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT scan of the abdomen and pelvis following the
intravenous administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque .  Coronal and sagittal
reformatted images were also generated for review.

FINDINGS:

portions of the heart and pericardium are unremarkable.  There is no pleural
effusion.

LIVER:  The liver demonstrates heterogeneous attenuation and a nodular contour
more compatible with cirrhosis.  There is a recanalized paraumbilical vein.  A
1.6 cm hypodense lesion is seen in segment II compatible with recent TACE
site.  The main portal vein is patent.  Patient is status post cholecystectomy
with mild prominence of the common bile duct measuring up to 11 mm which
tapers to normal caliber as it enters the ampulla.

stranding or fluid collection.

SPLEEN  The spleen is homogeneous and normal in size.

ADRENALS:  The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

GI TRACT:  The stomach, duodenum, and small bowel are within normal limits,
without evidence of wall thickening or obstruction.  The colon remains mostly
collapsed and not fully evaluated.  The appendix is chronically dilated with a
